root_idea.summary: The root centers on connection or attachment between one thing and another, especially connection through lineage or relationship.
root_idea.development: This notion extends from kinship and tracing origins to attribution, proportion, correspondence, and a continuous or connected path; poetic nasīb is understood as speech connected to the beloved.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular dictionary citation form نَسَبٌ; the group includes the Quranic plural surface أَنسَابَ as well as نَسَبًا.

senses.definition: Kinship or blood relationship through one or both parents; lineage or family connection.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic usage covers both vertical lineage through ancestors and descendants and lateral kinship between related families. In the construction نَسَبًا وَصِهْرًا, it denotes kinship by parentage as distinct from affinity by marriage; the plural surface form أَنسَابَ denotes such relationships collectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To state, identify, or trace a person's relationship, lineage, or affiliation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May identify descent from an ancestor or affiliation with a tribe, city, district, craft, or profession; it may also be used to ask someone to state his lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refer the origin, derivation, or name of a person or thing to a source; to attribute or ascribe it to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an explicit object of attribution and may concern the origin of a name, an object, or an idea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impute, charge, or accuse someone of a fault or other act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional accusatory use, distinct from simply identifying lineage or origin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mention a woman in amatory language or describe her in the opening of a poem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A poetic construction used for the amatory prelude before the poem turns to its main subject; it includes descriptions of beauty, youth, affection, or related themes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To share a relationship with someone or be related to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III construction expresses reciprocal or shared relationship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To correspond to, resemble, suit, or befit someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for resemblance, analogy, conformity, correspondence, or suitability rather than genealogical kinship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the wind, to become violent and drive dust and pebbles along.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the specific construction describing a violent wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To claim or assert that one is a relation or kinsman of another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The claim may be made toward a specified person and need not itself establish that the relationship is genuine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be mutually related, similar, corresponding, or suitable to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes reciprocal relation, resemblance, analogy, conformity, or fitness between two or more things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be proportionate, symmetrical, or uniform in one's parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used when the components of something are suitably related in size, arrangement, or structure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assert or claim relationship or descent from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of claiming relationship to one's father, whether truthfully or falsely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be attributed or ascribed to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested for a voice or utterance whose source is assigned to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To state or disclose one's own relationship, lineage, or genealogy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in a request that a person identify his lineage so that others may know him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go back and forth between two parties spreading malicious misrepresentations, calumnies, or slanders.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized quadriliteral usage describing the transmission of hostile allegations between two people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relative, kinsman, or person sharing a relationship, including one related through marriage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can designate a male or female relation and a person who becomes related by marriage; an old commentary citation associates this kinship interpretation with Quranic discussion, but no modern verse location is asserted here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person of rank, quality, or distinction who is also of notable family or lineage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Combines social standing or quality with family or lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An elegant amatory mention of a woman or women at the beginning of a poem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The poetic genre or passage of nasīb concerns love, longing, and description of the beloved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A highly skilled genealogist or a person exceptionally knowledgeable in genealogies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive professional or laudatory description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A straight, direct, conspicuous, or narrow road or track; by extension, an uninterrupted line or trail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a road, the traces of a road, a continuous procession of ants, or the tracks of a serpent or wild asses going to water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most elegant in the style of poetic nasīb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative expression applied to poetry judged especially effective in its amatory prelude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Regular or standardized in form, especially of handwriting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is explained as properly named or characterized in relation to an author or established rule.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A poem containing a nasīb, or amatory passage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the poetic composition rather than to a person's lineage or attribution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relation, proportion, or comparison between quantities or measures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for the proportional relation of one quantity to another, including expressions such as the proportion of ten to a hundred.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name or designation of relation to a parent, tribe, place, district, craft, or profession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes relational adjectives ending in ـِيّ, such as a designation connecting someone with a tribe, town, or occupation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Resemblance, similarity, conformity, analogy, correspondence, or suitability between things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the relation between two things when they resemble, correspond to, or suit one another.

cautions: The Quranic group combines the plural surface أَنسَابَ with the singular accusative نَسَبًا; the public headword is normalized to نَسَبٌ.
A historical commentary citation attached to the نَسِيبٌ entry is retained as lexical context for kinship, but its printed notation is not converted into a modern verse location.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The citation “Jel, xxv. 56” in the نَسِيبٌ discussion does not securely identify a supplied QAC occurrence and may reflect historical citation or transcription conventions; its kinship interpretation is represented without assigning a modern verse key.
